subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core/provider-runtime Anthropic pace projection and any automatic throttling for autonomous agents, and which surface should own the default behavior?
rationale: The request adds provider-specific usage semantics, persisted state, new config, and autonomous blocking behavior that can affect auth routing and session continuity, so code automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Visibility First
options.body: Add pace projection to provider usage/status/session_status without default blocking so operators and agents can self-regulate first.

options.title: Opt-In Throttling
options.body: Design an explicit agents.defaults pace policy with persisted state and focused upgrade/session-safety tests before blocking subagents or non-interactive work.

options.title: Defer To Plugin/Skill
options.body: Keep core closed until a missing plugin/provider API seam is identified, leaving external pace tools to own policy for now.

recommendation.title: Visibility First
recommendation.body: Add pace projection to provider usage/status/session_status without default blocking so operators and agents can self-regulate first.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored the current provider usage/status and cooldown surfaces that would need the first scoping decision.
